References / Poster / 446

Drive (2011 film), US theatrical poster

The US poster for Nicolas Winding Refn’s Drive: a sunlit photograph of Ryan Gosling and a huge hot-pink brush-script title on a white border.

Source
IMP Awards: Drive (2011)
Creator
FilmDistrict (distributor); designer not credited on the source
Made
2011; film released in the US on 16 September 2011 (Wikipedia)
Style
Synthwave (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Cinematic, nostalgic, tense
Evidence
Inspected the 1000 × 1500 poster image from IMP Awards in a scratch folder. Not stored. This is the “Some heroes are real” one-sheet with the 09.16.11 date, not the steering-wheel poster in the Wikipedia infobox.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: Drive was directed by Nicolas Winding Refn and released in the United States on 16 September 2011. “While Drive is set in the present day, it has a 1980s atmosphere, underlined by the vehicles, music, and clothes, and by the architecture.” Its hot-pink opening credits were inspired by Risky Business (1983), and the credits play over Kavinsky’s “Nightcall”. Wikipedia).

The synthwave record lists Drive among the works that spread the look. Wikipedia says that Hotline Miami (record) took inspiration from it, and that James White, who drew the Blood Dragon key art (record), had made artwork for the film.

Observed

  • A white sheet frames a tall, warm photograph of a man in a dirty white T-shirt seen from below, against a hazy pale-yellow sky, with a concrete bridge at the lower right.
  • The title “Drive” is set very large in a hot-pink, rough-edged brush script. It overlaps the bottom of the photograph and runs out onto the white border.
  • “SOME HEROES ARE REAL” runs vertically up the left margin in small, widely spaced thin capitals.
  • “IN THEATRES 09.16.11” sits at the bottom in wide-spaced italic gray capitals.

Why it belongs

The poster shows where the hot-pink script came from: a daylight, film-poster gesture that later synthwave covers moved onto a black night ground and lit as neon. On its own it fails the rubric’s counter-sign of a light ground.

Borrow

Set one short word very large in a hot-pink brush script, overlapping the edge of the image it names.
